size.note: Length 0.50-0.65 m, wingspan 0.81-0.98 m, 0.7-1.6 kg (drakes heavier). The floating bird is scaled to 0.58 m bill tip to tail tip; the origin is at the WATERLINE: the flat underside 0.04 m below it, the back 0.10 m above it, the crown 0.22 m; the broad flat bill 0.052 m from its base, ~2.4 cm wide; the legs reach 0.084 m below the waterline; wing cards 0.90 m tip to tip. The drake (_COLORB) is drawn on the same mesh (the client may scale him about 1.05x).

source.prompt: (the merganser's) A common merganser (Mergus merganser), adult female, swimming low on the water, side-on pose, wings folded, NOT a mallard, NOT a duck with a broad flat bill. No water modelled: the bird alone with a flat waterline underside. Realistic proportions: 62 cm long, a long low streamlined body, a long thin straight red bill with a small hooked tip, a rusty chestnut head with a shaggy crest hanging back from the nape, a sharp line between the rusty neck and the white chin and breast, a grey back, flanks and tail. No base. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: The merganser's floating body made a dabbler: the neck shortened 55% over its middle and thickened 1.3x, the head 0.86x (rounder: 1.06x across) on it, the body 1.12x across, the wing tips and tail behind the rump shortened 0.7x and cocked up; the thin bill cut off and a broad flat spatulate bill built in its place (a five-sided tube of sections, 6 / 4 / 3 sections per tier); the drake's two small curled black central tail feathers (lod0, the hen's tail colour on her), a dark eye (lod0), orange legs with webbed feet, wing cards. Triangles: lod0 1,199 = 998 body + 201 bill, legs, cards, eyes and curls; lod1 449 = 358 + 91; lod2 149 = 88 + 61. GLB 303,504 bytes.

rig: bird rig template exactly as client/assets/merganser.glb (tools/build_merganser.py; a swimmer: y = 0 is the waterline), to be loaded with the merganser's constants: PART BODY 0, LEG_A 1 (left) / LEG_B 2 (right) short legs pivoting at the hip (under the water while it swims; for a walk on the bank the client raises the bird by extras.rig.feet_y_m = -0.084), TAIL 3 (tail, crossed wing tips and the drake's curls; pivot at the tail root), HEAD 6 = neck, head and bill pivoting at the neck's base (a dabble or an up-ending swings it down), WING_L/R 4/5 arm cards (pivot at the shoulder) and HAND_L/R 9/10 hand cards (pivot at the wrist) that collapse into the shoulder at rest (collapse 1). extras.rig keys (the merganser's): kind 'bird', wing [0.048, 0.088, 0.186], tail [0, 0.052, -0.118], head [0, 0.081, 0.272], hip [0.027, -0.005, 0], length_m 0.58, span_m 0.9, waterline_m 0, draft_m 0.04, feet_y_m -0.084, variant 'breeding drake in _COLORB (the hen in COLOR_0)'. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a mallard pair at every tier. Hen (COLOR_0): mottled brown and buff all over (hashed dark centres and buff edges), a dark brown crown and a dark eye line, a paler buff face and throat, an orange bill with a dark saddle, the blue speculum bordered white on the folded wing and the cards, orange legs. Drake (_COLORB): glossy green head (two greens hashed), a white neck ring, chestnut breast, pale grey vermiculated flanks and back, black rump and undertail, the black curls, a yellow bill. Still open: the body is the merganser's and still a little long and low for a mallard (the fuller width helps from above, less from the side); the neck ring is jagged on lod0 (whole decimated faces) and may vanish on lod2; the hen's eye line and crown are coarse face patches; the drake's tail is black with a pale tip where a real drake shows whitish outer tail feathers; the curls are thin tubes on lod0 only; the bill is a separate tube pushed into the face (no seam blend), a touch long-looking from the side; the speculum on the folded wing is a painted band on the flank faces. A local birder should check the bill shape and the head size on the water.
